title: Minnesota AG Sues Texas Gov. Abbott to Compel Extradition of ICE Agent Castro
excerpt: Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison filed a federal lawsuit against Texas Governor Greg Abbott on August 18, 2026, seeking to compel the extradition of ICE agent Christian Castro, who faces felony assault and false-reporting charges for a January 2026 shooting in Minneapolis. Abbott had refused to sign the extradition warrant for nearly three months.
content:
On August 18, 2026, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison sued Texas Governor Greg Abbott in federal court after Abbott refused for nearly three months to sign an extradition warrant for ICE agent Christian Castro.

  • Castro was arrested in Cameron County, Texas, on May 29, 2026, after being charged in Minnesota with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime.
  • Castro is accused of firing his gun through the front door of a Minneapolis home during Operation Metro Surge, wounding a man in the leg, and then falsely accusing the victim of attacking an ICE officer to justify the shooting.
  • Minnesota Governor Tim Walz sent a formal extradition request to Abbott in early June 2026. Abbott had signed similar warrants from Minnesota in an average of 30 days in other cases but took no action in Castro's case.
  • Ellison warned that Castro faced imminent release from his Texas jail under the state's 90-day limit, with prosecutors fearing he could flee to Mexico from the border town where he was held.

The lawsuit marked an unprecedented interstate legal confrontation over the accountability of a federal immigration agent. Two other ICE agents involved in Operation Metro Surge remained under state investigation, while the federal government continued to block state access to evidence in the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti.

"Christian Castro is not above the law, and Greg Abbott isn't, either," Ellison said at a news conference announcing the suit.
source: Minnesota Attorney General / NPR / Washington Post
